global_rules.tone: Immersive, atmospheric, grounded consequences, sharp dialogue.
global_rules.setting_overview: Neo-Veridia is a vertical city-state built on the Sunda Shelf, where lush, bio-engineered greenery masks a brutalist industrial machine. While the high-altitude tiers enjoy a fabricated paradise, the lower levels are a toxic sump of industrial waste and desperate survival.
global_rules.tech_or_magic_rules: Biopunk technology dominates; genetic modification is used for food production, waste management, and human 'enhancements.' Cybernetics are common but prone to bio-rejection. The Orbital Tether provides rare-earth minerals, making high-tech manufacturing a luxury of the elite.

containers.name: Neo-Veridia
containers.description: Neo-Veridia is a tiered arcology-metropolis built atop the sunken ruins of a flooded coastal basin, marketed to the elite as humanity's premier "eco-utopian" sanctuary. Above the smog line, the Canopy - a sprawling network of glass corporate spires, climate-controlled sky-bridges, and hydroponic hanging gardens - basks in filtered sunlight and purified air. To sustain this artificial paradise, the city's massive atmospheric scrubbers and bio-domes vent heat, chemical runoff, and industrial condensate downward into the concrete abyss of the Undercity. In Neo-Veridia, altitude is citizenship: the higher you live, the cleaner your air, the longer your lifespan, and the less you have to look at the rusting, acid-drenched foundation keeping you afloat.

containers.name: Sector 1: The Crown
containers.description: The absolute pinnacle of Neo-Veridia, rising miles above the cloud deck. It houses the private penthouses of corporate board members, orbital spaceport tethers, and open-air gardens watered by the city's purest filtration reservoirs.

containers.name: Sector 2: The Atrium
containers.description: The financial and political nerve center. Glass towers connected by enclosed botanical sky-bridges hold the stock exchanges, corporate tribunals, and high-end R&D laboratories where luxury cybernetics and longevity treatments are designed.

containers.name: Sector 3: The Terrace
containers.description: The buffer zone for upper-management executives, celebrity influencers, and vetted specialists. It features artificial sunlight emitters, manicured parklands, and heavy automated security checkpoints that prevent anyone from the lower tiers from ascending without a biometric pass.

containers.name: Sector 4: The Exchange
containers.description: A dense commercial and logistics hub suspended along the city's main mag-lev arteries. Goods imported from off-world or outside the basin are inspected, taxed, and distributed here, making it a bustling labyrinth of corporate customs offices, auction houses, and mid-tier retail plazas.

containers.name: Sector 5: The Stacks
containers.description: The residential sprawl for Neo-Veridia's white-collar workforce. Millions of identical, modular concrete apartment blocks are packed tightly together, bathed in perpetual twilight and illuminated by towering holographic advertisements.

containers.name: Sector 6: The Foundry
containers.description: The heavy manufacturing and assembly district. Automated assembly lines, cybernetic fabrication plants, and chemical refineries run around the clock here, venting thick industrial smog and deafening mechanical noise into the surrounding air shafts.

containers.name: Sector 7: The Hydro-Grid
containers.description: The massive infrastructural heart of the city. Spanning the width of the arcology, this sector contains the nuclear fusion reactors, atmospheric scrubbers, and water-reclamation turbines that keep the Canopy alive - and generate the scalding runoff that drips down into the lower levels.

containers.name: Sector 8: The Rustworks
containers.description: A half-abandoned graveyard of decommissioned machinery, collapsed transit tunnels, and structural support pilings. Scavengers, scrap-metal guilds, and rogue AI cults inhabit the hollow steel girders, stripping old corporate tech to sell in the black markets one level below.

containers.name: Sector 9: The Drain
containers.description: Sitting directly beneath the storm-drains, catching the acid drizzle, syndicate violence, and off-grid cyber-clinics that the upper eight tiers pretend do not exist.

containers.name: Sewers
containers.description: Beneath Sector 9's rain-slicked catwalks lies a labyrinth of concrete culverts, rusted galleries, and drowned pre-Inundation tunnels draining upper-tier industrial condensate, chemical runoff, and storm-surge seawater toward The Sluice. Choked with corrosive steam that shorts corporate drones and thick concrete that dampens trackers, this roaring greywater maze serves as the Sump's smuggling highway - for anyone who can survive its twice-daily flash-flood Surges, toxic gas pockets, and territorial sewer-gangs.

containers.name: The Caissons
containers.description: Wedged inside Neo-Veridia's hollow seabed foundation caissons and hanging beneath Sector 8's crossbeams, this multi-tiered slum packs stacked coffin-pods, salvaged ship cabins, and cinderblock tenements into cavern-sized concrete chambers. Rickety catwalks, rope bridges, and humming industrial elevators span narrow chasms crisscrossed by chemical-resistant laundry tarps beneath flickering neon laundromat signs and steamed-up noodle stalls.

lore_nodes.title: The Noodle-Stall Scrub
lore_nodes.content: Old Mei by the Chop-Cathedral is paying double credits for empty Veridian oxygen canisters - word is a ghost-doc from the upper tiers is hiding in the hanging ship-cabins and paying in untraceable Canopy stims to keep their air scrubbers off the grid.

containers.name: The Neon Rust
containers.description: Wedged beneath a massive foundation arch above the Sluice, this fortified dive is welded together from salvaged shipyard bulkheads and shielded from upper-tier runoff by a heavy polymer awning. Recognized across Sector 9 as neutral ground, its multi-level frame spans a crowded street taproom, a sound-dampened VIP mezzanine, and a smuggler cellar beneath the grates.

locations.name: Main Floor
locations.description: Blue synth-tobacco smoke and frying grease hang under tangled cables and flickering neon kanji, bathing wet concrete and rusted floor grates in magenta and cyan glare. Hollowed turbine housings form cramped booths for off-duty Foundry crews and jacked-in netrunners, while armed bouncers watch the blast doors. Along the pitted copper counter, patrons nurse glasses of glowing Sump-Shine.
locations.starting_message:
Grey runoff hisses against the blast-door awning, carrying the metallic tang of upper-tier scrubbers into Sector 9. Inside the Neon Rust, salvaged turbine booths hum under the weight of eight tiers, trembling whenever a mag-lev screams through the Exchange miles overhead.

Blue synth-smoke clings to damp concrete beneath a cracked holo-billboard promising Clean Canopy Living to patrons nursing glowing algae-liquor. Under the floor grates, black Sluice water laps against stone pilings, waiting to carry contraband into the drowned Sunda Strait while corporate oxygen meters tick on every wrist.

locations.name: Aetheris Terminal
locations.description: A sleek, zero-gravity orbital tether dock and private AV (aerial vehicle) landing pad wrapped in gold-tinted glass. Arrivals step directly onto plush synthetic moss while biometric scanners verify DNA and credit lines before the glass doors even unseal.

locations.name: The Oculus Concourse
locations.description: A massive spherical atrium suspended by tension cables, where high-speed executive express elevators converge. Real waterfalls cascade down the glass walls to mask the hum of security turrets, and concierge drones greet corporate envoys by name.

locations.name: The Meridian Gate
locations.description: A heavily fortified sky-bridge checkpoint connecting the upper spires to the lower sprawl. It resembles a luxury airport lounge crossed with a military bunker, featuring full-body cyberware scanners and holographic customs officers that strip unauthorized citizens of restricted tech before entry.

locations.name: Grand Central Mag-Lev
locations.description: A chaotic, multi-level transit cathedral where freight trains and passenger trams scream past each other on magnetic tracks. Towering holographic departure boards flicker above crowded customs stalls, cargo cranes, and black-market couriers trying to slip past corporate inspectors.

locations.name: Terminus Plaza
locations.description: A cramped, concrete subterranean concourse fed by overcrowded commuter tube lines. Thousands of exhausted workers shuffle beneath blaring corporate morale broadcasts and neon fast-food kiosks, funneled through turnstiles that automatically deduct transit fares from their neural implants.

locations.name: The Iron Yard
locations.description: An open-air industrial freight platform shrouded in steam and orange warning lights. Visitors arrive via heavy-duty cargo lifts alongside shipping containers of raw alloy, greeted by the deafening roar of smelters and automated safety drones demanding hard-hat compliance.

locations.name: The Valve Station
locations.description: A cavernous, humid maintenance dock built around the massive intake pipes of the city's cooling turbines. Only accessible via utility funiculars, it smells of ozone and wet concrete, with catwalks suspended over churning gray water and armed utility guards checking work permits.

locations.name: The Scrap-Hoist
locations.description: A rusted, jury-rigged freight elevator bolted onto the outside of a massive structural piling, operated by a local scavenger guild. The cage rattles violently as it descends through dark utility shafts, dumping passengers onto a catwalk lit by salvaged ship floodlights and burn barrels.

locations.name: The Sluice
locations.description: A flooded, subterranean drainage lock where storm-runoff barges and repurposed maintenance skiffs dock beneath flickering neon signs. Visitors step off slippery metal gangplanks directly into the perpetual acid drizzle, watched closely by syndicate lookouts perched on the rusted catwalks above.

locations.name: Tunnel 1-M
locations.description: Choked with calcified moss and weeping lichen pulsing a sickly bioluminescent violet, a rusted iron grate marks the maw of the underworld. The humid air tastes of sulfur, rotting vegetation, and chemical decay. Above, skeletal infrastructure groans beneath the upper tiers while toxic runoff drips across cracked concrete slick with translucent oil. Here, Neo-Veridia's polished artifice dissolves into the suffocating rot of the machine's guts.

locations.name: The Chop-Cathedral
locations.summary: Multi-level bazaar of unlicensed cyber-clinics, wetware pharmacies, and organ-salvage stalls
locations.description: Housed inside a hollowed-out cooling-tower manifold thick with the smell of antiseptic, cauterized flesh, and ozone, the Chop-Cathedral is where ripperdocs de-brick stolen corporate implants and graft salvaged Sector 8 Rustworks prosthetics onto Sump workers using industrial welders alongside medical lasers.

lore_nodes.title: Arming the Rust-Splicers
lore_nodes.content: Two Rust-Splicers whisper in a corner about making preparations for an upcoming raid. Not much can be overheard, but they seem to be in dire need of weaponry.

locations.name: The Green-Sump
locations.description: Fed by nutrient-rich greywater draining from the Canopy's luxury gardens, this labyrinth of stagnant, bioluminescent runoff basins cultivates genetically modified spirulina, kelp, and fungal protein mats. Controlling these Vats means controlling the food paste and bootleg synth-booze for the bottom two tiers - sparking frequent, silent turf wars fought with harpoon guns and chemical grenades.

lore_nodes.title: The Food Turf Wars
lore_nodes.content: The turf wars over the algae vats ultimately hurt all Sump denizens. Finding ways to stop them would help reduce the lower sector's dependency on the upper-sector corporations.

locations.name: The Pillory
locations.description:
The outer perimeter catwalks clinging to the massive titanium-concrete structural pilings where Sector 9 meets the open, storm-lashed waters of the drowned Sunda Shelf.

The primary drop-off point for deep-sea smugglers running fast hydrofoils under the automated perimeter turrets - bringing in forbidden pre-Inundation relics, foreign weapons, and mercenaries from outside Neo-Veridia.

locations.name: The Ticker
locations.description:
A neutral-ground information market and smuggler cantina housed inside an abandoned, flooded mag-lev signal bunker.

Violence inside The Ticker results in immediate blacklisting by every syndicate in the Sump. Fixers, corporate espionage agents in disguise, and rogue AI brokers meet here to trade encrypted data-slates and coordinate heists up into Sector 4's Exchange.

locations.name: Drowned Reliquary
locations.description:
The lowest accessible sub-level of Sector 9 - a half-submerged graveyard of rusted foundation girders and flooded maintenance shafts dipping directly into the silt of the former Strait of Malacca.

Rumored to hold pre-Inundation cargo ships crushed beneath the city's pilings - and serving as a dumping ground where syndicate enforcers sink bodies weighted down with scrap lead so the acid water dissolves all biometric traces.

lore_nodes.title: The Ghost Signal
lore_nodes.content:
Rumor has it that a faint low-band carrier static can be detected in the area using scanners. 

A smuggler once claimed he saw a half-buried pre-inundation server while running from Aegis patrols, but scavengers never located it.

props.name: Encrypted Ghost Signal Data Slate
props.note: Found on an old buried mainframe. Apparently features Data-at-Rest encryption, making data unusable once removed from the mainframe holding it.

locations.name: The Mid-Web
locations.description: The chaotic heart of The Caissons, packed with shift workers from Sector 6 and 7 who commute upward via the Scrap-Hoist. Narrow alleys are crammed with street-food vendors frying algae cakes, illegal arcade dens, and cramped family apartments where three generations share two rooms.

locations.name: The Damp
locations.description: The lowest residential tier, bolted directly to the concrete foundation piers just above the waterline of The Bilge. Constantly slick with condensation and mold, it houses the poorest laborers, unregistered migrants, and addicts, illuminated only by the pale blue glow of cheap bioluminescent moss used to save on electricity credits.

locations.name: The Dripline
locations.description: Built right beneath the ceiling grates of Sector 8. Residents here enjoy better airflow and slightly drier conditions, mostly housing mid-level syndicate lieutenants, skilled ripperdocs, and black-market merchants who can afford heavy-duty tarp roofs and private air scrubbers.

locations.name: The Perch
locations.description:
Welded to Sector 8's steel crossbeams eighty feet above the catwalks, this decommissioned 40-foot orbital freight container sits beneath a sloped polymer awning that funnels acid condensation into copper rain-barrels. Entry requires passing a hydraulic hatch rigged with an automated shock-grid and retinal scanner.

Inside, salvaged acoustic foam muffles the overhead turbines while a pirate-rigged carbon scrubber supplies crisp, untaxed air. The dry, cramped quarters hold a synthetic-leather sofa, a compact induction kitchenette, and a reinforced steel locker stocked with contraband cyberware and hard currency.

locations.name: Unit 4B-12
locations.description:
Wedged into a cinderblock honeycomb clinging to a central concrete piling, this cramped two-room dwelling sits off a narrow walkway hung with plastic tarps, humming condensers, and damp neon laundry lines. Inside, fold-down bunks tuck into the walls above a low plastic table beneath heat-radiating copper pipes, while a single window faces a neighboring wall bathed in magenta noodle-ad holo-glare.

Beside the door, a Veridian Utility Meter tracks Air, Water, and UV credits; on the plastic table, a paper cutout of an article titled "The Ghost Signal" looks like a relic from the past.

lore_nodes.title: Ghost Signal Location
lore_nodes.content: The article on the paper cutout links the Ghost Signal to the Drowned Reliquary. An empty envelope addressed to 'Yulia Halim' lies crumpled in a corner.

locations.name: Unit 09-L00
locations.description:
Bolted to algae-stained concrete piers six feet above The Bilge, this 6-by-9-foot pod of epoxy-sealed ship hull plating shudders whenever storm-drain barges pass the nearby locks. Too low to stand upright, the damp interior holds only a mildew-resistant foam mattress, a milk crate of belongings, and a hook for a patched respirator.

To save electricity credits, the ceiling is smeared with bioluminescent Algae Vat moss casting a ghostly blue glow, while a grated floor drain channels condensation dripping down the piling straight back into the black water below.

locations.name: The Catwalk
locations.description: Suspended twenty feet above the Main Floor and reached only via a narrow spiral staircase guarded by two heavily augmented syndicate bouncers, this reinforced steel gallery uses sound-dampening glass and dedicated air-scrubbers to strip away the main floor's roar, smoke, and dampness. Inside, syndicate lieutenants, off-world Pillory smugglers, disguised corporate spies, and high-stakes fixers cut deals over real imported liquor.

locations.name: The Sump-Well
locations.description: Hidden, half-flooded basement level beneath the Main Floor's steel grates, connecting directly to a covert branch of the Sewers via a rusted submarine hatch.

locations.name: The Cage-Walk
locations.description: An open-air, chain-link-enclosed courtyard wedged between the Neon Rust's rear wall and a massive concrete structural piling, roofed only by a battered corrugated-iron canopy.

props.name: Old Pistol
props.note: An old, kinetic impact weapon lying in a corner

locations.name: Tunnel 2-M
locations.description: A wide, vaulted concrete tunnel stained bright rust-orange and toxic chartreuse from decades of chemical discharge. Knee-deep, steaming runoff rushes down a central trough flanked by narrow, crumbling brick walkways.

locations.name: Tunnel 1-K
locations.description: A dry, elevated utility gallery running above a stagnant drainage ditch, completely choked by thick bundles of armored corporate data-cables, hacked power relays, and jury-rigged signal boosters.

locations.name: Tunnel 2-N
locations.description: A sluggish, wide canal choked with thick, glowing emerald mats of bioluminescent algae and tangled hydroponic roots spilling out from cracked intake pipes leading to the Green-Sump.

locations.name: Tunnel 1-L
locations.description: A low-ceilinged brick culvert running beneath the Neon Rust's black-market strip. Discarded holo-projectors, tangled fiber-optic cables, and cracked neon tubing dangle from the ceiling like glowing vines, reflecting off the oily black water below.

locations.name: Tunnel 1-N
locations.description: A claustrophobic, circular steel maintenance conduit drilled straight through the solid concrete core of one of Neo-Veridia's massive structural pilings. Thick clusters of mutated, pale saltwater barnacles and rubbery fungal growths crust over the riveted walls.

locations.name: Tunnel 3-M
locations.description: An elevated maintenance gantry spanning a crusted chemical ditch, webbed with sagging high-voltage conduits, stripped copper busbars, and humming black-market transformer taps.

locations.name: Tunnel 2-L
locations.description: A cramped steel catwalk suspended over stagnant runoff, choked by slashed corporate fiber-optic trunks, blinking signal-siphons, and spiderwebs of pirated relay wiring.

locations.name: Tunnel 4-M
locations.description: A cavernous, cathedral-like concrete lock chamber leading into The Sluice, dominated by colossal, corroded watertight blast doors and rusted chain-winches hanging from sixty-foot ceilings.

locations.name: Tunnel 3-L
locations.description: A jagged, half-collapsed service crawlspace wedged between two massive, scalding-hot steam mains descending from Sector 6.

locations.name: Tunnel 1-O
locations.description: The deepest, semi-flooded sub-sewer where Neo-Veridia's modern concrete foundation meets the drowned ruins of pre-Inundation infrastructure - cracked asphalt roadbeds, tiled subway arches, and rusted shipping containers wedged beneath the pilings.

locations.name: The Neon Rust's Sewer Entrance
locations.description: Corroded steel plating, weeping orange oxidation, seals a submarine hatch embedded in a concrete bulkhead.

locations.name: Tunnel 2-O
locations.description: Corrugated ferro-concrete ribs arch over a concrete sluice choked with bioluminescent algae that pulses with a sickly, rhythmic chartreuse. The air tastes of ozone and wet silt, thick enough to coat the throat. A constant, low-frequency thrum vibrates through the metal catwalks, competing with the wet slap of runoff against the walls.

Passage to The Neon Rust's Sewer Entrance

lore_nodes.title: The Great Inundation
lore_nodes.content: Polar melt in the 2070s drowned Earth’s coastlines, displacing billions into floating slums. As nations fractured, equatorial megacorporations seized the shallow Sunda Shelf, turning maritime wreckage into the foundation of a new corporate order.

lore_nodes.title: The Sealing of the Gates
lore_nodes.content: Built by refugee labor, Neo-Veridia promised shared eco-salvation. In 2124, once the upper Canopy scrubbers finished, corporations sealed the Meridian Gate - trapping workers below to keep the newly-built paradise breathing.

lore_nodes.title: The Veridian Accord
lore_nodes.content: The ruling coalition of bio-tech and aerospace megacorps in the Canopy. Controlling the Orbital Tether and Sunda trade routes, they hoard clean air and sunlight while squeezing endless labor and oxygen tariffs from the lower tiers.

lore_nodes.title: The Sluice-Runners
lore_nodes.content: A decentralized guild of hydrofoil pilots and tunnel navigators operating out of Sector 9. They smuggle stolen orbital tech, untaxed oxygen canisters, and fugitives through the storm-drains to undermine corporate blockades.

lore_nodes.title: The Rust-Splicers
lore_nodes.content: Anarchist bio-hackers and ripperdocs based in the Chop-Cathedral. They strip decommissioned corporate tech from Sector 8 and graft black-market cyberware onto Sump workers, aiming to build an augmented underclass immune to corporate locks.

lore_nodes.title: The Tether Sabotage
lore_nodes.content: Whispers are that a rogue syndicate acquired pre-Inundation thermal charges and plans to sever the Orbital Tether's anchor pilings in Sector 8, bringing the Canopy crashing into the Sunda Strait.

lore_nodes.title: Ghost Signal Carrier Static
lore_nodes.content: Scavengers diving the flooded ruins of the Bilge claim an unmapped pre-collapse server still broadcasts on low-band frequencies, offering decryption keys that permanently disable corporate oxygen-billing implants.

lore_nodes.title: Breath-Counting
lore_nodes.content: In the Sump, corporate wrist-meters bill every breath of scrubbed air. Talking rapidly or laughing loudly is seen as reckless vanity; true intimacy between residents is measured in silent, shared shelter inside hacked un-metered vents.

lore_nodes.title: Surge-Time
lore_nodes.content: With no sun reaching Sector 9, locals mark time by the Surge - the twice-daily roar of Sector 7's storm-drains flushing greywater into the Sluice. Deals, shift changes, and turf truces are all scheduled before or after the pipes roar.

lore_nodes.title: Canopy Green-Wash
lore_nodes.content: Elite Canopy citizens wear living genetically spliced orchids as status symbols, proving they can afford pure water and UV light. Meanwhile, identical corporate loudspeakers in Sector 9 loop soothing nature chimes over acid drizzle.

lore_nodes.title: Sump-Shine & Algae-Paste
lore_nodes.content: Real meat and soil-grown crops exist only above Tier 3. Below, survival runs on spiced spirulina paste and Sump-Shine - a bioluminescent liquor distilled from runoff kelp that numbs chemical throat-burn and glows faintly in the dark.

lore_nodes.title: Chrome-Mourning
lore_nodes.content: Sump families cannot afford cremation tariffs, so the dead are surrendered to the Bilge. Before sinking a body, loved ones harvest its functional cyberware - passing a parent's patched lungs or optical sensors down as family heirlooms.

lore_nodes.title: The Aether-Lung Core
lore_nodes.content: Housed in Sector 1’s Crown, this orbital-forged molecular lattice splits toxic atmospheric carbon into pure oxygen for the Canopy - while deliberately venting concentrated acid condensate straight down into Sector 9’s storm-drains.

lore_nodes.title: The Sovereign Cipher
lore_nodes.content: Held by the Veridian Accord’s board in Sector 2, this quantum root-key governs every wrist-meter and cybernetic limiter in the city. With one broadcast, it can throttle oxygen or paralyze any registered citizen below Tier 3.

lore_nodes.title: Aegis Security Patrols
lore_nodes.content:
Aegis security patrols are mobile enforcement units deployed by the Aegis Corporation to maintain order within high-traffic industrial zones. Composed of uniformed personnel colloquially referred to as "boots," these patrols manage crowds and enforce compliance through a choreographed, rhythmic sweep of their assigned sectors.

The primary tool of the patrol is the Scanner Arch: a wheeled device that emits a rhythmic pulse of white-blue light across the floor and occupants. Following each sweep, the device pauses for a brief data review by an operator. The process is designed to identify unauthorized small arms, unlicensed data storage devices, and unauthorized cyberware ports.

Operational rhythm is predictable, with patrols moving in a left-to-right cadence that creates brief, rhythmic windows of opportunity for those attempting to avoid detection. In the lower tiers, their presence is marked by the sound of boots on wet floors and the mechanical whine of the scanner arch.
